questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about India's 7th National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity?
o: Among national targets, biodiversity-inclusive spatial planning and ecosystem restoration were the ones clearly identified as on track.
Technical coordination rested with the National Biodiversity Authority.
The report confirms that India will reach the 30 per cent area-based conservation goal by 2030.
Preparation was supported by UNDP under an umbrella programme of the Global Environment Facility.
questions.e: The report does not confirm reaching 30 per cent; protected areas cover only a little over 5 per cent of land, and other area-based measures are still being identified. The remaining statements are accurate. The National Biodiversity Authority coordinated technical work, and UNDP assisted under GEF-8. Only NBT-1 on planning and NBT-2 on restoration are clearly placed on track, while the other targets mostly list policies rather than projections, which is why observers call implementation through 2030 the real test.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 12-14; Vision IAS pp. 49-51

questions.q: The inaugural National Highways Green Cover Index, released by NHAI with ISRO's National Remote Sensing Centre, assesses roadside vegetation chiefly through
o: carbon-flux towers installed at intervals along national highways
satellite detection of chlorophyll content using Resourcesat-2/2A and Cartosat-2S sensors
ground tree counts by highway concessionaires, audited by the Forest Survey of India
aerial LiDAR surveys that estimate tree height and biomass along each corridor
questions.e: The index uses high-resolution satellite data to pick up chlorophyll, with Resourcesat and Cartosat-2S sensors, so that green cover change can be tracked yearly. It is not a field count, so the Forest Survey and concessionaires do not generate the figures. LiDAR and flux towers are real tools for biomass and carbon exchange, but neither underlies this index. The approach is scalable and repeatable across a large network without any ground enumeration, and it gives highway authorities a measurable greening metric.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 57

questions.q:
With reference to access and benefit sharing in India, consider the following statements:
1. Biodiversity Management Committees are State-level bodies that approve access by foreign entities.
2. Under the Nagoya Protocol, access to genetic resources rests on the provider's Prior Informed Consent, and benefit sharing on Mutually Agreed Terms.
3. An Internationally Recognised Certificate of Compliance serves as evidence that a resource was accessed in line with these requirements.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Consent and agreed terms are the twin pillars of the Protocol, with compliance as the third obligation. Certificates published in the global system create a traceable record, and India has about 60 per cent of the world's total. Statement 1 is wrong: the committees operate at the local level. The national tier is the National Biodiversity Authority, and the State tier comprises State Biodiversity Boards and UT Councils, under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 51-52

questions.q:
Statement-I: A flood-generating glacial hazard in the Himalaya can arise today even without a lake outburst or a cloudburst.
Statement-II: Loss of seasonal snow and firn leaves glacier ice exposed, so that it fragments and melts faster.
Statement-III: Steep gradients and narrow valleys can turn a small ice collapse into a fast debris surge.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: All three are correct, and both later statements explain the first. Snow and firn normally insulate the ice below, so their loss exposes it to rapid decay, partly because erratic Western Disturbances have reduced winter snow. Slopes above about 35 to 40 degrees then give fallen ice enormous energy. The Dharali event illustrated this combination, which is why ISRO's study called exposed ice patches an under-recognised risk and urged detection through multi-temporal satellite imagery such as Sentinel-2.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 53-54

questions.q:
During Chennai's 2019 water crisis, four reservoirs that together met about 60 per cent of the city's demand fell below 1 per cent of capacity. Of the following reservoirs:
1. Poondi
2. Chembarambakkam
3. Mettur
4. Cholavaram
how many were among those four?
questions.e: Poondi, Chembarambakkam and Cholavaram were among the four, the fourth being Red Hills. Item 3 is wrong: Mettur stands on the Cauvery in Salem district and is not one of Chennai's local reservoirs. The crisis followed about 200 days without rain and was worsened by the loss of over 2,000 of the 6,000 lakes and reservoirs in the three 'Yeri districts'. It is often cited to argue that 'Day Zero' is a failure of governance as much as of rainfall.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 76-79; Mettur location is static

questions.q: In discussions of urban water supply, 'non-revenue water' refers to
o: treated wastewater supplied free of charge to industries
rainwater harvested by households that is not billed by the utility
groundwater drawn by private tankers beyond municipal control
water put into the network that earns no revenue because of leaks, theft or unbilled use
questions.e: Non-revenue water is the gap between what a utility supplies and what it bills. Causes include leaking and ageing pipes, illegal connections and metering errors. In Delhi nearly half of supply reportedly falls into this category, which aggravates a large demand-supply gap. It is not related to free recycled water, household rainwater harvesting or private tankers, although tankers tend to thrive where network losses leave shortages. Reducing it is a core part of urban water budgeting because it adds supply without a new source.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 76-79

questions.q:
Among the measures counted towards India's NDC, consider the following pairs:
Programme : Focus
1. MISHTI : Mangrove restoration
2. Nagar Van Yojana : Urban forests
3. Perform, Achieve and Trade : Energy efficiency in energy-intensive industries
4. Green India Mission : Improving forest quality and expanding forest and tree cover
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four pairs are correct. MISHTI targets mangrove plantations along the coast, while Nagar Van creates forests in urban areas; both add to the carbon sink and to adaptation. Perform, Achieve and Trade lets efficient units in energy-intensive sectors sell savings certificates to those that fall short. The Green India Mission, one of the NAPCC missions, aims at better forest quality and more tree cover. Rooftop solar, a common distractor here, belongs instead to PM Surya Ghar.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 47-48; scheme focus for Nagar Van and Green India is static

questions.q:
Which of the following best distinguishes the two reports that India submitted under the Convention on Biological Diversity process?
1. The 7th National Report assesses progress on national targets aligned with the global biodiversity framework.
2. The first national report on the Nagoya Protocol assesses access and benefit sharing, and it feeds into Target 13 of India's NBSAP.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Both are correct and they should be kept apart. The first document is a broad review of 23 national targets and 142 indicators under the NBSAP 2024-30. The second is narrower: it records approvals, certificates, and money flowing to communities through benefit sharing. It connects with the broader plan through Target 13, which deals with genetic resources. A common error is to credit the certificates figure to the 7th report, or the forest cover and species data to the Nagoya report.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 49-52; Shankar IAS pp. 12-14

questions.q:
With reference to small hydro power in India, consider the following statements:
1. In India, hydro plants of up to 25 MW are classed as small hydro.
2. The 'mini' class of hydro projects is larger in capacity than the 'small' class.
3. Small hydro falls under the Ministry of Power, while large hydro falls under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The class sequence by capacity runs micro up to 100 kW, mini up to 2 MW, and small from 2 to 25 MW, which makes statement 2 wrong. Statement 3 reverses the ministries: small hydro sits with MNRE, which approved the new scheme for 2026-27 to 2030-31, while large hydro is under the Ministry of Power. Small plants are usually run-of-river or on canal falls and dam toes, and the threshold also matters for clearance exemptions under EIA rules.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 54-55; large hydro under Ministry of Power is static

questions.q:
Statement-I: Warming in the Himalaya threatens yields of apples and cherries in the region.
Statement-II: These fruit trees need a period of winter chilling to flower and fruit properly.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and the second explains the first. Temperate fruit trees need a fixed accumulation of cold hours to break dormancy. Warmer winters deny them this, which brings poor flowering and yields and also earlier pest outbreaks. Water stress adds to the problem as snowfall declines. This is one of the less obvious effects of deglaciation, which also include altered river flows, damage to hydropower assets, and cascading disasters. Mountain agriculture is therefore treated as part of climate adaptation planning.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 53-54

questions.q:
On India's energy-efficiency framework, consider the following statements:
1. The Energy Conservation Sustainable Building Code is aimed at commercial buildings, while Eco Niwas Samhita is aimed at residential buildings.
2. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency is a statutory body created under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, and functions under the Ministry of Power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The two building codes are separated by use: commercial structures under the sustainable building code and homes under Eco Niwas Samhita. The Bureau, which marked its 25th foundation day, was created by the 2001 Act under the Ministry of Power, not the Environment Ministry. It runs Star Labelling and the Perform, Achieve and Trade scheme for energy-intensive industries. The same Act later supplied the legal basis for carbon trading, which is why energy efficiency law now connects with climate policy.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 47-48, 57

questions.q:
With reference to the draft amendment to the EIA Notification, 2006 issued by MoEFCC in March 2026, consider the following statements:
1. A proposed Standing Authority on Environment Impact Assessment would act in place of a State Environment Impact Assessment Authority that is non-functional or causing delay, for a period of up to one year.
2. The draft proposes to abolish State Expert Appraisal Committees and route all State-level proposals permanently to the central Expert Appraisal Committee.
3. A proposal not appraised by a State Expert Appraisal Committee within 120 days would shift automatically, through the PARIVESH portal, to a proposed Standing Committee on Environment Impact Appraisal.
4. The draft was issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. The draft, issued under the 1986 Act, creates standing bodies in each State that step in for a stalled SEIAA or SEAC for at most one year, with a 120-day trigger and automatic transfer through PARIVESH. Statement 2 is wrong and in fact describes the present fallback the draft seeks to replace: today the central Expert Appraisal Committee absorbs a State's workload when its bodies lapse, often because their three-year tenure ends without timely reconstitution.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 45-47

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is correct?
o: It was notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and is administered by the Central Pollution Control Board.
It replaced the Paris Agreement's Article 6 mechanisms for all Indian companies with a domestic voluntary scheme.
It was notified under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 and obligated sectors are given greenhouse gas intensity-reduction targets.
It sets absolute emission caps for each obligated entity, in the manner of the European cap-and-trade system.
questions.e: The scheme was notified in 2023 under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, and it forms the base of the Indian Carbon Market. Intensity targets are fixed by rules for sectors such as refining, cement and aluminium, and firms beating them earn tradable credits. It was not issued under the 1986 Act and is not run by the pollution board. It sets no absolute caps, in line with India's intensity approach. It also does not displace Article 6, which is an international cooperation route.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 47-48, 57

questions.q:
Statement-I: Earth's energy imbalance can widen even in a period when countries are cutting aerosol pollution.
Statement-II: Many aerosols reflect incoming sunlight, so their reduction allows more solar energy to be absorbed by the climate system.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. Sulphate-type aerosols scatter sunlight and partly mask greenhouse warming. Cleaner air therefore removes some of that cooling shield, adding to the gap between energy received and energy radiated to space. WMO's State of the Global Climate 2025 listed reduced aerosols among the causes of the imbalance, alongside higher greenhouse gas levels and lower reflection by clouds and sea ice. This is the so-called aerosol paradox: a public health gain can have a short-term warming cost.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 56-57

questions.q:
With reference to India's updated Nationally Determined Contribution for 2031-35, consider the following statements:
1. The updated NDC commits India to a dated phase-out of coal-based power generation.
2. Under the Paris Agreement, communicating an NDC is an obligation, though meeting its targets is not enforceable as a legal duty.
3. Because India's headline mitigation target is expressed as emissions intensity of GDP, absolute emissions could still rise while the target is met.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Paris design is procedural: Parties must submit a contribution every five years, but compliance relies on transparency and peer pressure. An intensity target measures emissions per unit of GDP, so a growing economy can emit more in total; India defends this on equity grounds, given low per-capita emissions. Statement 1 is wrong: the update contains no fossil phase-out date, and observers point to plans for new coal capacity as a risk of carbon lock-in.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 47-48; Shankar IAS pp. 70-73

questions.q: Earth's energy imbalance, which WMO listed among key climate indicators for the first time in its 2025 report, is best understood as
o: the difference between net solar energy received by the Earth and the long-wave energy it radiates back to space
the imbalance between ocean heat uptake and land surface heat release during El Nino
the gap between global energy demand and renewable energy supply in a given year
the temperature difference between the two hemispheres, averaged across a decade
questions.e: The imbalance equals incoming solar radiation less the reflected part, minus outgoing long-wave radiation. A positive value means that the planet is accumulating heat, while a negative value means cooling. It is thus a measure of the rate of heat gain, and many scientists view it as more comprehensive than surface temperature, since most of the excess goes into the oceans. The other descriptions confuse it with the energy economy, with hemispheric contrast and with a single El Nino effect.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 56-57

questions.q:
In the context of the Supreme Court's ruling in M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India on corporate environmental responsibility, consider the following statements:
1. The Court drew on the Fundamental Duty in Article 51A(g) to link the right to do business with a duty towards ecosystems.
2. Companies whose activities threaten the Great Indian Bustard's habitat were held liable to fund both in-situ and ex-situ conservation.
3. The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposes to lower the net-profit trigger for CSR applicability from Rs 5 crore to Rs 1 crore.
4. The statutory CSR spend under the Companies Act, 2013 is computed on the average net profit of the three preceding financial years.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Court treated CSR as carrying an inherent environmental duty, invoking Article 51A(g) and the Polluter Pays Principle, so firms harming bustard habitat must bear recovery costs inside and outside its natural range. Section 135 fixes the spend at 2 per cent of the three-year average net profit. Statement 3 reverses the direction: the Bill proposes raising the net-profit trigger to Rs 10 crore, which would take smaller companies out of the mandate.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 73-75; Section 135 is static

questions.q:
With reference to the World Meteorological Organization, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is headquartered at Nairobi as a subsidiary organ of the UN Environment Programme.
2. World Meteorological Day is observed on the anniversary of the adoption of the Paris Agreement.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Neither is correct. The WMO is a specialised agency of the United Nations based at Geneva; Nairobi hosts UNEP, a different body, and both sponsored the IPCC. World Meteorological Day, on 23 March, recalls the coming into force of the WMO Convention in 1950. The Paris Agreement was adopted in December 2015. The 2026 observance used the theme 'Observing Today, Protecting Tomorrow', and the organisation released its State of the Global Climate report on that occasion.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 56-57; WMO status and 1950 Convention are static

questions.q: The principle of 'absolute liability', laid down by the Supreme Court in the Oleum gas leak case (M.C. Mehta v. Union of India, 1987), differs from the older English rule of 'strict liability' mainly because
o: it applies only to damage caused by government agencies
it requires the claimant to prove negligence by the enterprise
it allows no defences such as act of God or act of a third party to an enterprise engaged in hazardous activity
it limits compensation to the actual value of damaged property
questions.e: Absolute liability goes further than the rule in Rylands v Fletcher. An enterprise running a hazardous or inherently dangerous activity must compensate for harm caused, and the exceptions that strict liability recognised do not apply. Negligence need not be proved, so that description is reversed. The rule covers private industry and not just state bodies, and compensation is not capped at property value, as courts may scale it to the enterprise's capacity. It supports the polluter pays approach in Indian law.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 58; Oleum gas case and Rylands v Fletcher comparison are static

questions.q:
With reference to the assessment of glacier loss in the Hindu Kush Himalaya by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), consider the following statements:
1. The Karakoram lost a larger share of glacier area than the Ganga basin between 1990 and 2020.
2. The Ganga basin lost a larger share of glacier area than the Brahmaputra basin over that period.
3. Glaciers larger than 10 sq km were found to be shrinking fastest.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct: the Ganga basin lost about 21 per cent and the Brahmaputra about 16 per cent. Statement 1 is wrong because the Karakoram remained relatively stable, with about 2 per cent loss, a known regional anomaly. Statement 3 is wrong because the smallest glaciers, those below about half a square kilometre, are shrinking fastest; little ice mass means quick response to warming. ICIMOD also reports that melting has doubled since 2000.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 53-54

questions.q:
Regarding landmark environmental rulings, consider the following pairs:
Case : Principle or outcome
1. T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad : 'Forest' read widely to cover all recorded forest areas irrespective of ownership
2. Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum : Precautionary and Polluter Pays principles treated as part of Indian environmental law
3. M.K. Ranjitsinh (2025) : Definition of forest under the Van (Sanrakshan) law
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Godavarman read 'forest' beyond its classified meaning to cover all areas recorded as forest, whoever owns them, which widened central control over diversion of such land. Vellore declared the two named principles part of Indian environmental law, and they also underpin impact assessment. Pair 3 is wrong: the 2025 Ranjitsinh ruling dealt with corporate social responsibility and recovery of the Great Indian Bustard, not with the definition of forest. Keep each holding tied to its case.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 45-47, 58; Shankar IAS pp. 73-75

questions.q:
Which of the following are described as exempt from the EIA requirement in India?
1. Solar and wind power projects
2. Strategic highway projects within 100 km of the international border
3. Hydro projects of 100 MW capacity
4. Biomass-based thermal plants of up to 15 MW using an eco-friendly fuel mix
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Items 1, 2 and 4 are exempt. Solar and wind have been kept out, border highways get relief on strategic grounds, and small biomass-based plants are spared if they use the specified fuel mix. Item 3 fails because the hydro exemption applies only to plants below 25 MW, the same line that defines small hydro. Critics say widening exemptions dilutes appraisal: the cumulative effect of several projects in a fragile area may be serious even when each unit stays under the cut-off.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 45-47

questions.q:
Statement-I: India's EIA process does not formally examine the effects of a project on neighbouring countries.
Statement-II: India has not ratified the Espoo Convention of 1991.
Statement-III: The Espoo Convention is a protocol under the Convention on Biological Diversity.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statement-I reflects a gap identified in India's system, and Statement-II gives the reason: India stays outside the treaty on assessment in a transboundary context, so it has no matching obligation. Statement-III is wrong because Espoo arose under the UN Economic Commission for Europe and is unrelated to the CBD, whose protocols are Cartagena and Nagoya. The matter is relevant for shared Himalayan rivers. India's own draft reform focuses on reducing State-level delays rather than on the cross-border dimension.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 45-47; UNECE origin is static

questions.q: In the context of the global biodiversity targets, 'Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures' best describes
o: off-site facilities such as seed banks and captive-breeding centres
buffer zones around tiger reserves in which all human activity is prohibited
legally notified national parks and wildlife sanctuaries that have received a management-effectiveness rating
areas outside formal protected areas that deliver lasting in-situ conservation, whatever their primary purpose
questions.e: OECMs are sites such as sacred groves or certain community or defence lands which conserve biodiversity in practice even though conservation need not be their main aim. They count alongside protected areas towards the 30x30 goal, which is why India, with just over 5 per cent under protected areas, is identifying them. Notified parks are protected areas and not OECMs, buffer zones allow regulated activity, and seed banks are ex-situ, whereas OECMs must conserve nature in place.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 12-14; OECM examples are static

questions.q:
With reference to the 2030 targets of the Kunming-Montreal Framework, consider the following statements:
1. The 30x30 target covers land, inland waters and marine areas.
2. It seeks to halve the overall risk from pesticides and highly hazardous chemicals.
3. It seeks to halve the introduction of invasive species.
4. It calls for all harmful subsidies to be fully eliminated by 2025.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The 30x30 goal extends to terrestrial, inland water and coastal or marine zones, with a parallel goal to restore 30 per cent of degraded ecosystems. The pesticide-risk and invasive-species goals are each framed as a halving. Statement 4 overstates matters: the text calls for cutting harmful subsidies by at least USD 500 billion a year by 2030, not eliminating them by 2025. The finance goals, too, run to 2030, with interim figures for 2025.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 12-14; Vision IAS pp. 49-51

questions.q: According to Central Water Commission estimates for 1985-2023, which one of the following river basins has the highest average annual water availability in India?
questions.e: The Brahmaputra leads at about 592 billion cubic metres, narrowly ahead of the Ganga at about 582, with the Godavari a distant third at about 129. Many assume the Ganga is first because of its larger basin area and population, but the Brahmaputra's short Indian course receives very heavy rainfall. More than two-thirds of India's water comes from the three Himalayan transboundary systems, and this raises the stakes of China's proposed mega dam on the Yarlung Tsangpo and other shared-river questions.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 76-79

questions.q:
Statement-I: Environment-related work receives the largest share of CSR spending by Indian companies.
Statement-II: Land-based restoration projects are slow to show results and need specialised expertise that many CSR partners lack.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is wrong: education leads with about 38 per cent, followed by healthcare at about 22 per cent and rural development at about 10 per cent, leaving the environment with some 7 to 9 per cent. Statement-II is correct and is part of the reason for that low share. Firms prefer quick, easily reported activities over planting and soil recovery, which need ecological skill. Critics also point out that fast Miyawaki plantations can look good while harming native ecology.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 73-75

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Entry into force of the Nagoya Protocol
2. Enactment of India's Biological Diversity Act
3. Launch of the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund
4. Adoption of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The correct sequence is the Biological Diversity Act of 2002, followed by the Nagoya Protocol taking effect in 2014, after adoption in 2010. The Kunming-Montreal framework then came at COP-15 in 2022, and its dedicated fund was launched at Vancouver in 2023. The order matters conceptually: India's domestic law predates Nagoya and later became its implementing vehicle through the three-tier structure, while the fund could arise only after the framework it finances had been agreed.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 49-52; Shankar IAS pp. 12-14; 2002 Act date is static

questions.q:
Scientists say erratic Western Disturbances are reducing core winter snowfall in the Himalaya. Which of the following statements about Western Disturbances is/are correct?
1. They originate over the Bay of Bengal as tropical depressions moving north-west.
2. They bring winter precipitation to north-western India, including snow on the Himalaya.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Western Disturbances are extra-tropical storms from the Mediterranean region, carried eastward by the westerlies, so statement 1 confuses them with monsoon depressions. They provide winter rain and snow, which matter for wheat and for building up the seasonal snowpack. If this pattern weakens or shifts, the insulating snow and firn cover on glaciers thins, ice becomes exposed, and melt speeds up. The change therefore links atmospheric circulation with cryospheric hazards like the one at Dharali.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 53-54; origin is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs, based on the First Water Bodies Census:
State : Leads the country in
1. West Bengal : Tanks
2. Andhra Pradesh : Lakes
3. Tamil Nadu : Ponds and reservoirs
4. Maharashtra : Water conservation schemes
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 4 is correct. The census placed West Bengal first in ponds and reservoirs, Andhra Pradesh first in tanks, Tamil Nadu first in lakes, and Maharashtra first in water conservation schemes. Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are therefore shuffled. The exercise, the first of its kind, counted over 24 lakh water bodies. It also showed the system to be overwhelmingly rural and small in scale, with very few bodies having large water-spread or storage, which shapes how revival schemes must be designed.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 76-79

questions.q:
With reference to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted at COP-15 of the Convention on Biological Diversity and succeeded the Aichi Biodiversity Targets.
2. Its 30x30 target is legally binding on every Party to the Convention.
3. The Global Biodiversity Framework Fund created to support it is managed by the Global Environment Facility.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The framework was adopted in Montreal in 2022 and replaced the Aichi Targets of 2011-2020. Its fund was launched at the GEF's Seventh Assembly at Vancouver in 2023 and is run by the GEF, with a share earmarked for Indigenous peoples. Statement 2 fails because the framework as a whole is non-binding: Parties translate its 23 targets into national plans such as India's NBSAP, and rely on reporting and review rather than enforcement.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 49-51; Shankar IAS pp. 12-14

questions.q: Which one of the following describes the term 'sponge city', suggested as a response to urban water crises?
o: A city in which reservoirs are desilted annually to raise their capacity
A city that imports treated water from distant basins during peak summer demand
A city that meters every connection to bring non-revenue water to zero
A city designed with permeable surfaces, green spaces and recharge systems so that rain is absorbed and stored
questions.e: The idea is that a city should behave like a sponge: green areas, permeable paving and rainwater harvesting let water soak in and recharge urban aquifers, limiting both floods and shortages. Long-distance import is what such cities try to reduce. Metering addresses losses and is a separate reform under water budgeting, while desilting is a storage measure. After day-zero style crises at Shimla, Chennai and Bengaluru, the concept is promoted as an element of climate-resilient governance.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 76-79

questions.q:
With reference to the three India-China border trade passes, consider the following statements:
1. The Sutlej enters India at Shipki La.
2. The Brahmaputra enters India through Nathu La.
3. Lipulekh lies close to the India-China-Nepal tri-junction.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh is the point where the Sutlej crosses from Tibet. Lipulekh in Uttarakhand lies near the tri-junction, which gives it a sensitivity with Nepal too. Statement 2 is wrong: Nathu La is a Sikkim pass linking to Tibet's Chumbi side and has no connection with the Brahmaputra, which enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang. These three passes are the designated points for resuming India-China border trade, and each has a distinct geography.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 58; Brahmaputra entry and Nathu La setting are static

questions.q:
In the context of the Falkenmark indicator, often cited to describe India's falling water availability, consider the following statements:
1. NITI Aayog's projection of about 1,140 cubic metres per person a year by 2050 would place India below the indicator's threshold for water scarcity.
2. The indicator measures only the groundwater extracted in a basin, per hectare of irrigated land.
3. It is calculated by the Central Water Commission from household water bills.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. On the Falkenmark scale, availability below 1,700 cubic metres per person per year signals stress and below 1,000 signals scarcity, so 1,140 would mean stress, not scarcity, and statement 1 fails. Statement 2 is wrong because the index relates renewable water availability to population, not groundwater to farmland. Statement 3 is wrong as it is a simple per-capita measure named after hydrologist Malin Falkenmark, not a bill-based official computation. About 820 million Indians are already near or below 1,000.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 76-79; Falkenmark method is static

questions.q:
Statement-I: India's CO2 emissions grew at the slowest pace since 2001 in 2025, leaving aside the pandemic year.
Statement-II: Clean power additions covered most of the rise in electricity demand in 2025.
Statement-III: Mild weather and weak industrial demand restrained energy use in 2025.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: All three are correct, and both later statements explain the first, according to analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air published by Carbon Brief. Solar, wind, hydro and nuclear additions pushed power-sector emissions down, while mild weather and soft demand helped. The analysts caution that a single year is not a trend, particularly as steel and cement emissions rose sharply. So the finding shows a possible turning point in power, not an economy-wide peak in emissions.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 70-73

questions.q: According to India's 7th National Report to the CBD, the largest share of India's forest carbon stock is held in
questions.e: About 55 per cent of the forest carbon stock of roughly 7,285 million tonnes is soil organic carbon, which surprises many who picture trees as the chief store. Above-ground biomass, roots, dead wood and litter together make up the rest. The point has policy meaning: land-use change that disturbs soil can release long-held carbon, so protecting old forest is not equivalent to fresh planting. It also explains why restoration success is now measured through soil carbon and other ecological indicators.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 49-51

questions.q:
Consider the following plant species:
1. Chromolaena odorata
2. Prosopis juliflora
3. Mimosa diplotricha
4. Shorea robusta
5. Terminalia arjuna
How many of the above were flagged in India's 7th National Report to the CBD as invasive species spreading in tiger-range States?
questions.e: Chromolaena odorata, Prosopis juliflora and Mimosa diplotricha were flagged, with Chromolaena reported to have expanded by about 70 per cent; they crowd out native fodder and so weaken the prey base for carnivores. Shorea robusta (sal) and Terminalia arjuna are native Indian trees and not invasive aliens. Invasive species also matter under the global framework, whose targets include halving the rate at which they are introduced and established by 2030.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 49-51; native status of sal and arjun is static

questions.q: In the context of Digital Sequence Information, which came up alongside benefit sharing in the global biodiversity framework, which one of the following is the most appropriate description?
o: Genetic data, such as DNA and RNA sequences, that can be used without physically handling the source organism
A blockchain ledger of carbon credits generated by biodiversity projects
Electronic permits that sequence approvals for international wildlife trade
Satellite-based digital maps recording the sequence of forest loss over a region
questions.e: Digital Sequence Information refers to genetic sequence data held in databases. It creates a policy puzzle: companies can use it to develop products without collecting the plant or animal, so consent-based access rules do not easily apply. The global framework therefore calls for fair sharing of benefits from such data. Forest maps, wildlife trade permits and carbon ledgers are unrelated. The matter is important for a megadiverse country like India, which wants custodians of biodiversity to gain from its use.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 12-14; definition is static

questions.q:
On India's international climate partnerships, consider the following pairs:
Initiative : Associated fact
1. International Solar Alliance : Launched by India and France in Paris in 2015
2. Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure : Secretariat in New Delhi
3. Leadership Group for Industry Transition : Launched with India and Sweden as leading countries
4. Global Biofuel Alliance : Launched during India's G20 presidency
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four are correct. The solar alliance began at COP-21, with its secretariat at Gurugram. CDRI was announced by India in 2019 and is based in New Delhi. LeadIT was launched by India and Sweden at the 2019 UN Climate Action Summit to help heavy industry decarbonise. The biofuel alliance came at the New Delhi G20 in 2023, with Brazil and the United States among the founders. India's NDC documents count these partnerships as part of its international climate action.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 47-48, 52-53; origin details are static

questions.q:
On global water governance, consider the following statements:
1. The term 'water bankruptcy' was introduced in UN-Water's World Water Development Report 2026.
2. The UN Water Conference 2026 is co-hosted by the Netherlands and Tajikistan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. The water bankruptcy framing comes from UNU-INWEH, which argued that withdrawals beyond renewable replenishment make 'stress' too mild a word, while the UN-Water report this year focused on water and gender. The 2026 conference is co-hosted by the UAE and Senegal, and prioritises water in multilateral processes. The Netherlands and Tajikistan co-hosted the earlier 2023 conference, which is the source of the common confusion. All of this sits within the Water Action Decade of 2018-2028.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 76-79; Vision IAS p. 55; 2023 co-hosts are static

questions.q:
In the context of similarly named international instruments, consider the following pairs:
International instrument : Main concern
1. Bonn Challenge : Restoring degraded and deforested land
2. Bonn Convention : Conservation of migratory wild animals
3. Espoo Convention : Transboundary movement of hazardous wastes
4. Nagoya Protocol : Safe handling of living modified organisms
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The Bonn Challenge is a voluntary land-restoration pledge, whereas the similarly named Bonn Convention is the Convention on Migratory Species. Pair 3 is wrong: Espoo deals with environmental impact assessment in a transboundary context, and India has not ratified it; hazardous waste movement falls under the Basel Convention. Pair 4 is wrong: Nagoya covers access to genetic resources and benefit sharing, while living modified organisms fall under the Cartagena Protocol, also a CBD supplement.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 45-47, 51-52, 55; Shankar IAS pp. 73-75; Basel and Cartagena are static

questions.q:
Consider the following States/UTs:
1. Sikkim
2. Arunachal Pradesh
3. Meghalaya
4. Nagaland
How many of the above are named as high-risk under the National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme?
questions.e: Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh are named, along with Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh. Meghalaya and Nagaland are not, as they lie outside the high glaciated Himalaya and their risks are rainfall-driven landslides and floods. The programme is under the National Disaster Management Authority, with its first phase over 2023-26. Glacial lake outbursts come from moraine-dammed lakes breaching, so geography rather than general hill status decides the list, and that is what the question tests.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 53-54

questions.q:
Which of the following statements with regard to global climate pledges are correct?
1. UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2025 places full implementation of current NDCs on a path of more than 2 degrees Celsius of warming.
2. Analysis by WRI and E3G finds that no NDC contains a full fossil-fuel phase-out plan.
3. The UAE Consensus reached at COP-28 included a call for transitioning away from fossil fuels and tripling renewable capacity.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All three are correct. UNEP's 'Off Target' report estimates 2.3 to 2.5 degrees under pledges, far from 1.5. WRI and E3G found mostly partial transition goals, with subsidy reform largely absent. The COP-28 outcome called for tripling renewables and moving away from fossil fuels, but national pledges have not fully reflected this. Taken together these support the view that NDCs often record progress rather than drive it, with the renewables boom owing more to falling costs and industrial competition.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 70-73

questions.q:
In the context of humid heatwaves, consider the following statements:
1. Rossby waves are large meanders in the atmosphere that owe their existence to the Earth's rotation, and their stalling can hold hot, humid air over a region.
2. At the same dry-bulb air temperature, drier air has a higher wet-bulb temperature than more humid air.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Rossby or planetary waves arise from the Earth's rotation and land-sea temperature contrasts, and when a wave train stalls it traps a heat dome; a March 2026 study linked this to humid heatwaves. Statement 2 is wrong because the relation runs the other way. Wet-bulb temperature reflects how much evaporative cooling is possible, and moist air allows less of it. That is why humid heat is more dangerous to the body than dry heat at the same thermometer reading.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 59

questions.q: The term 'nivation', which appeared in the news after a study on a Himalayan flash flood, best refers to
o: basal melting of a glacier caused by heat rising from the underlying bedrock
erosion of the ground beneath and around a snow bank, chiefly through alternate freezing and thawing
the deposition of rock debris by a retreating glacier to form a moraine-dammed lake
the compaction of multi-year snow into dense granular firn at the top of a glacier
questions.e: Nivation is the wearing away of ground under and around a snow patch as meltwater repeatedly freezes and thaws; it can deepen hollows on a mountainside. The other descriptions name different processes: firn is old snow on its way to becoming ice, moraine dams form from glacial debris and can later burst, and basal melting is a glacier-bed process. ISRO placed the failed ice patch at Srikanta in such a nivation zone, a setting not usually watched by warning systems.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 53-54; firn and moraine are static

questions.q:
Statement-I: India's non-fossil sources account for more than half of installed electricity capacity, yet a much smaller share of electricity actually generated.
Statement-II: India's NDC target on non-fossil power is defined in terms of the share of electricity generated in a year.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: non-fossil capacity crossed 50 per cent, but generation stays below about 30 per cent, with coal still near 55 per cent. Solar and wind run at lower utilisation than coal, so capacity overstates their output. Statement-II is wrong because the NDC target is set on installed capacity, not generation. This distinction is the key criticism of the metric, and it is why storage and hybrid solar-wind systems are stressed as the next step for decarbonisation.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 47-48; Shankar IAS pp. 70-73

questions.q:
Match List-I (Report or declaration) with List-II (Body responsible):
List-I
A. 'Off Target' Emissions Gap Report 2025
B. World Water Development Report 2026
C. Global 'Water Bankruptcy' declaration
D. State of the Global Climate 2025
List-II
1. UN University Institute for Water, Environment and Health
2. World Meteorological Organization
3. UN Environment Programme
4. UN-Water
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Emissions Gap series is UNEP's and found current pledges close only a small part of the gap. The World Water Development Report is issued for UN-Water and this year centred on water and gender. The stronger term 'water bankruptcy', meaning withdrawals beyond renewable replenishment, came from UNU-INWEH, a UN University unit, so it is easy to misattribute to UN-Water. The State of the Global Climate comes from WMO, on World Meteorological Day, and it added the energy imbalance as an indicator.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 55, 56-57; Shankar IAS pp. 70-73, 76-79

questions.q:
India's 7th National Report to the CBD counts 58 tiger reserves, 33 elephant reserves and 18 biosphere reserves. In this regard, consider the following statements:
1. Biosphere reserves are notified under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.
2. Tiger reserves have statutory backing under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, through its 2006 amendment.
3. Elephant reserves are statutory protected areas declared under the same Act.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The 2006 amendment inserted a chapter on the National Tiger Conservation Authority, under which States notify tiger reserves on its advice. Statement 1 is wrong: biosphere reserves are a programme category linked to UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere network, with no listing in the 1972 Act. Statement 3 is wrong because elephant reserves are administrative units under Project Elephant, so the land inside them takes protection only from whatever parks or sanctuaries it contains.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 49-51; legal basis of reserve categories is static

questions.q:
Match List-I (Himalayan disaster) with List-II (trigger generally identified):
List-I
A. Chamoli, 2021
B. South Lhonak, Sikkim, 2023
C. Dharali, 2025
List-II
1. Glacial lake outburst flood
2. Rock-ice avalanche
3. Collapse of an exposed ice patch
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Chamoli 2021 began with a massive rock and ice detachment from a Rishiganga catchment peak. The 2023 Sikkim disaster came when South Lhonak lake breached and sent a flood down the Teesta. The ISRO study on Dharali pointed to an exposed ice patch of the Srikanta Glacier failing, neither a cloudburst nor a lake outburst. Together they show why planning centred only on glacial lakes is too narrow: deglaciation creates a family of cascading hazards in steep valleys.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 53-54; event triggers for Chamoli and Sikkim are static

questions.q: The 'Solar Constancy Problem', mentioned among the challenges before the International Solar Alliance, refers to
o: year-to-year variation in the Sun's radiation owing to the sunspot cycle
the output gap at night and in poor weather, which raises the need for costly storage
the inability of member countries to keep solar tariffs constant
the fall in solar panel output as panels age over time
questions.e: The issue is intermittency: panels yield nothing at night, and less under cloud or pollution, so round-the-clock supply demands batteries many developing members cannot afford. Panel ageing and the solar cycle are real but minor and are not what the phrase refers to, and tariff stability is a different policy matter. Alongside this, the Alliance contends with insufficient public funds, private investors' perception of risk, weak local manufacturing, and high tariffs on cells and modules in some African and Pacific states.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 52-53
